highlights.title: Review: Godzilla Minus Zero joins the list of truly stellar sequels
highlights.summary: It's a rare thing for a film sequel to match or even surpass its predecessor; The Godfather Part II and Terminator 2: Judgement Day are the best known examples on a pretty short list. Go ahead and add Godzilla Minus Zero to that list.
body: As I wrote previously, Yamazaki wanted to return to Godzilla’s filmic roots with Minus One, setting the events in postwar Japan and tapping into the monster’s symbolic representation of the Japanese perspective on the 1940s nuclear holocaust—while also incorporating all-too-human themes of guilt and redemption. That first film focused on kamikaze pilot Kōichi Shikishima (Ryunosuke Kamiki), who struggled with survivor’s guilt after he failed to take action when Godzilla attacked the Japanese base on Odo Island in 1945.

Knocked unconscious, Kōichi survived and awoke to find his parents and many others were killed in the World War II bombing of Tokyo. Kōichi rebuilt a life with a woman named Noriko (Minami Hamabe) and the orphaned baby she rescued, Akiko (Sae Nagatani). But then Godzilla re-emerged, and Kōichi resolved to die fighting the monster to atone for Odo Island. Kōichi saved the day and lived to tell the tale. He reunited with Noriko, who had a strange black bruise on her neck. And we saw a chunk of Godzilla’s remains start to regenerate, leaving things open for a sequel.
points: It's a rare thing for a film sequel to match or even surpass its predecessor; The Godfather Part II and Terminator 2: Judgement Day are the best known examples on a pretty short list.
Go ahead and add Godzilla Minus Zero to that list.

highlights.title: 61 Years Later, Charlie Brown's Greatest Enemy Is Still an Undefeated 'Peanuts' Icon
highlights.summary: Like many comics aimed at children, Charles Schulz's Peanuts doesn't have too many actual villains. It has a number of antagonists, such as Lucy Van Pelt, various other kids, or the impersonal cloud of failure that constantly hangs over Charlie Brown's head, but it's rare to see a genuinely…
body: One of Charlie Brown's long-standing hobbies in Peanuts was kite-flying, despite not being very good at it. Whenever he tried it, he invariably got his kite caught in trees and/or himself wrapped up in the kite string. Like every other hobby in Charlie Brown's life, he was devoted to it despite his bad luck.

That hobby eventually introduced Charlie Brown to his nemesis. The Kite-Eating Tree was an otherwise unidentified tree in Charlie Brown's neighborhood that seemed to deliberately grab and eat his kites, to the point where Charlie Brown developed a one-sided rivalry with it.

According to Schulz in the autobiographical collection My Life With Charlie Brown (2010), the inspiration for the Kite-Eating Tree was simply a bit of observational humor. Schulz had noticed that a kite that got stuck in a tree would slowly disappear over the course of several weeks, as wildlife and the elements took their toll. He decided that must've been because the tree was eating the kite, and so the Kite-Eating Tree ended up in Peanuts.
The Kite-Eating Tree was first specifically identified in March 1965, which marked the beginning of a recurring story that would last for the next 30 years.

highlights.title: Clash Royale recruits creator of AI cheating tool to help catch cheaters
highlights.summary: Clash Royale developer Supercell has recruited the creator of an advanced AI cheating tool to help crack down on cheating in the game.
body: AI cheating has become a growing controversy in Clash Royale, with increasingly sophisticated bots reportedly capable of outperforming skilled human players. Players highlighted claims that an AI-controlled account named ‘Clasher’ had reached the top of the game’s global leaderboard.

The situation prompted calls for Supercell to intervene, with the developer addressing the controversy on November 20. In a statement posted on X, Clash Royale warned that using AI or other tools to cheat was a “royal crime,” declaring that offending players would be banished from the Arena.
On November 21, the official Clash Royale X account announced that it had caught the creator of an AI cheating tool and recruited them to help develop new anti-cheat technology.

“The creator of the AI cheating tool has been caught,” Supercell announced in a statement framed as a royal decree from the King. “He’s agreed, entirely of his own free will, to join forces with the Clash Royale team.

highlights.title: Amazon is complaining about NYC Council on shipping labels, too
highlights.summary: Amazon is leaving no venue unexplored in its fight against the New York City Council and the Delivery Protection Act. The company is now putting labels on shipments claiming that the Council could add up to $5 to any Amazon order.
body: Amazon is taking its accusations that the Council is driving up prices offline and onto your packages.

Earlier this week, Amazon started showing notifications in its mobile app and on its website reading “Attention NYC Council could add up to $5 per order.” Now the company is including an almost identical message on shipping labels.

Amazon claims that the bill, if passed, “would likely mean slower and more expensive delivery for millions of customers in New York City,” and has threatened to move its warehouses outside of the city. However, labor unions, Council Speaker Julie Menin, and Mayor Zohran Mamdani have countered that the company is attempting to “threaten New Yorkers and intimidate this City Council” and is acting out of “greed,” pointing to Amazon’s market cap of nearly $3 trillion.

highlights.title: The Outages Are Just Getting Started
highlights.summary: AI is forcing companies to patch their systems faster as attackers race to exploit newly discovered vulnerabilities. Welcome to internet outage hell.
body: Over the last week, you have surely noticed the disruptive streak of technical outages that hit everything from Outlook to Apple, a half dozen US banks, United Airlines, and even the NSA’s classified network. While there’s no evidence that these were cyberattacks, speculation has run wild about the cause—including a pervasive feeling that AI is to blame.

So let’s just be clear: The incidents were definitely not caused by some sort of coordinated AI hacking spree and, taken individually, they all seem to have routine explanations. But as AI impacts the dynamics of digital defense more and more, security researchers and analysts have increasingly concluded that AI pressures are starting to play a role in real-world tech failures.

highlights.title: 8 Must-Play JRPGs for People With Real-Life Schedules
highlights.summary: It’s 9:15 on a Wednesday night. The dishes are done. You have about 45 minutes before bed, and you’re a JRPG fan (or you were, when you had more time). JRPGs tend to demand dozens of hours from players — and they can make it very difficult to pause, as some of them will interrupt you with a battle…
body: But there are some games in the genre you can bend to fit your week. These eight JRPGs split their stories into chapters, let you switch off random battles, speed up fights, or save almost anywhere. Even if you press start at 9:20, you can still be in bed by 10.

This game opens with a disaster: the Great Chasm swallows a village, and a shepherd named Tiz is the only survivor. You play as Tiz, who teams up with Agnes, a vestal of the Wind Crystal, to free four elemental crystals that darkness has swallowed. Edea, a defector from the Eternian Sky Knights, and Ringabel, an amnesiac who carries a journal that seems to record future events, join the party along the way.

This remaster explicitly hands you the controls for your schedule. You can set the encounter rate from 50 to 200 percent at any time on the field map, push battle speed to 4x, and let auto-battle repeat your last actions. Turn the dial to match whatever time and energy you happen to have when you’re ready to play.

highlights.title: The 8 Best James Bond Films
highlights.summary: As we await Robert Pattinson’s first outing as 007, these are the classics worth revisiting now.
body: Terrible puns. Rampant misogyny. Disposable female characters. A frequently stale rotation of vodka martinis, gun fights, and stiff-upper-lip bureaucracy. Bond movies are very easy to make fun of—and, let’s face it, of the 25 that have so far been released over the past six decades, a majority are pretty forgettable. But there are a handful that are worth watching, even if you actively abhor the subgenre.
Following Robert Pattinson’s appointment as the new 007, we present eight Bond films that are actually decent. May more follow!

Where it all began. A suave Sean Connery, Ursula Andress as the bikini-clad Honey Ryder, the pristine white beaches of Jamaica… this Terence Young-helmed first installment of the franchise laid the blueprint for everything that followed, but is also a thoroughly entertaining romp in its own right. It’s easy to see why it became a box-office bonanza and birthed a cultural phenomenon that endures to this day.

highlights.title: Two groups verify mathematician’s claim that Claude helped prove mathematics problem
highlights.summary: Anthropic’s Levent Alpöge says it took six weeks for him using the AI tool to solve 19th-century Riemann hypothesis. A mathematician at Anthropic has said that the San Francisco -based artificial intelligence (AI) company’s software has helped crack one of the most important unsolved problems in…
body: Levent Alpöge, a Turkish American mathematician, on Friday posted a note on his personal website saying that Claude, the AI software, had helped prove the Riemann hypothesis. He says that Claude helped develop a solution to the problem during the course of about six weeks.
On Saturday afternoon, two organizations announced that they had independently verified Alpöge’s claim after reviewing the programming language he used to share the solution.

The proof evidently marks another breakthrough in the use of AI for complicated math problems – even as mathematicians express uneasiness around extremely lucrative private companies dishing out millions of dollars for the technology to solve problems.

“Claude and I have had a great time together with such breadth in recent months, but this time Claude far outpaced me near the finish line,” Alpöge wrote, while anthropomorphizing the AI software. “No, Claude flew, and danced, and sparkled near that finish line.”

highlights.title: Signal restricts mobile screenshots as it confronts ‘existential threat’ of AI surveillance
highlights.summary: Signal is limiting users' ability to take screenshots in both its Android and iOS apps.
body: Signal announced Friday that it’s limiting users’ ability to take screenshots within the secure messaging app — a response to what President Meredith Whittaker described as the “existential threat” of operating systems that integrate agentic AI.

Whittaker wrote that by giving AI agents the ability to “scan” the information on users’ screens, Windows, Android, and macOS/iOS “are undermining Signal’s ability to independently guarantee privacy.”

“Now, in service of AI agentic capabilities, your sensitive data is being captured, stored, and made accessible to whatever local database or remote server an OS-level AI agent is using at that moment,” she said. “All of this is outside of Signal’s control once the data has been captured, and imperils the privacy of all the participants in a conversation.”
Signal already sought to limit these risks by blocking screenshots of its Windows app by default. Now it’s adding similar restrictions in Android and iOS.

highlights.title: Star Trek Reboot Officially Teased as Crimson Tide Meets Training Day Sci-Fi Thriller
highlights.summary: After more than a decade of waiting, it seems we may finally get a new theatrically released Star Trek movie. While dedicated Trekkies have heard that before, the directors of the only known Star Trek movie in development recently shared details about their project.
body: Specifically, they cited Training Day and Crimson Tide as jumping-off points for what they’re going for.

For those unfamiliar with Training Day, it stars Ethan Hawke as a newcomer LAPD narcotics officer under the tutelage of the corrupt detective Alonzo Harris, played by Denzel Washington. As for Crimson Tide, it’s a thriller about a U.S. nuclear submarine facing off against a Russian ultranationalist faction threatening to launch nukes at the U.S. and Japan (interestingly enough, it also stars Washington).

Past Star Trek movies have dealt with Starfleet bad apples before to varying levels of success, including Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country, Star Trek: Insurrection, and Star Trek Into Darkness. But Daly and Goldstein have another twist on the Star Trek formula.
“It takes place almost in real time, and it just is a whole other look at what a Star Trek movie could be without betraying the fundamentals of what it should be,” Daley said.

body: “I know we’re not here to talk about this, but I’m still grieving the end of ‘Succession,’” said Holden, to which Culkin responded: “Oh, you are? Get over it. It’s been three years!” When asked about a potential for a spinoff, Culkin answered, “Of course not. I think that would be a terrible idea… I mean, what are you hoping for? ‘Cousin Greg: The Sitcom?’… Yeah, that would be a terrible idea.”
And though the “A Real Pain” actor is steadfast about not retreading the show’s familiar territory, he noted that he misses playing Roman Roy and the “whole thing.”

Culkin continued: “It was fun. It was one of those where Jesse Armstrong, the showrunner, spent the entire last season trying to figure out if there was a way to do one more. I never wanted to know what was going to happen in the season and on the fourth one I did ask and when he pitched me the end of the season and I went ‘well, that kind of sounds like it’s the end of the show.’ But when he pitched me three different ideas of what season 5 could be, they all sounded good… But it ended perfectly. highlights.summary: One of the items on the agenda for UN diplomats meeting in Geneva this week was working towards rules regarding the use of autonomous weapons, or so-called "killer robots." Eventually, representatives left the meetings agreeing to "start discussing options" after a largely fruitless week of…
body: Before the negotiations got underway, the International Committee of the Red Cross, the guardian of the Geneva Conventions, said it was urgent for legally binding rules to be drafted within a year. That call was backed by the U.N. secretary-general and by Pope Leo.

The compromise reached was that countries would instead have two years to propose regulations. Negotiations between countries on which regulations to adopt and how to enforce them will likely drag on well beyond that. Additionally, room was left for some of those yet-to-be-adopted regulations to remain “optional.”

Humanitarian organizations and some countries see a need to urgently adopt legally binding rules as semi-autonomous weapons and drones have been responsible for a significant number of civilian deaths in conflicts around the globe, including in Ukraine, Gaza, and Sudan.
On day one, Russia delayed proceedings by objecting to the meeting’s agenda. Then the United States proposed a five-year window to discuss nonbinding, optional guidelines for autonomous weapons.

body: Rather than downloading another app, a growing number of agents can simply be texted like an ordinary person.

You text it what you need, and it can remember context, connect to the apps and services you already use, and complete tasks on your behalf. That can mean scheduling an appointment, organizing a calendar, researching a trip, sending an email, making a reservation, shopping online, or reminding you about something days later.
While Instinct is one of the buzziest AI agents at present, thanks to its $10 billion valuation after its latest funding round of $1 billion, there are many others also making a play for this space.
Ask Proxy ’s biggest differentiator is that it “thinks like a woman,” meaning it aims to anticipate your needs before you even ask, the company explains on its website.

highlights.summary: The Binding of Isaac developer Nicalis has removed undisclosed AI-generated music included in Repentance+ after backlash led to a review-bombing campaign on Steam and a response from the game's creator, Edmund McMillen.
body: McMillen and Nicalis spent months building up to the November 19, 2026, release date for the latest update in their classic action roguelike game, but that launch was quickly soured. Just 8% of The Binding of Isaac: Repentance+'s recent Steam reviews are positive, with a good chunk of comments left by players referencing AI-generated material that was not previously mentioned in any official capacity.
"Thanks, Nicalis, for breaking everything and adding AI slop to an already-existing game!" one popular review said.

"I'm starting to think that adding AI to a game should be valid grounds to refunds to people who have already paid for and played a game," another said. "Shameful they would do this to an Indie gem. Shameful."

The allegedly AI-generated content in question seems to be music exclusively tied to a specific, Grand Theft Auto-themed run meant to coincide with the recent release of GTA 6. What could have been a cute jab at another gaming titan boiled into a full-blown controversy for Nicalis when Reddit user ShweetsStuff reported the questionable tunes just one day after launch.

highlights.title: The Australian fashion artisans who still make clothes by hand
highlights.summary: The meticulous process of hand-stitching clothing and footwear is rare in Australia, but the ateliers who do so are attracting a new generation of clients and colleagues. Get our weekend culture and lifestyle email.
body: In a world where garment makers are forced to wear AI-training headgear and T-shirts can be ordered from Kmart on Uber Eats, it may seem as if the days of procuring something made by hand from an artisan are numbered.

While jobs in Australian textile, clothing and footwear manufacturing have been in freefall since their 1989 peak – from 115,000 to approximately 30,000 in 2026 – the work of a dressmaker or shoemaker who stitches every piece by hand is even harder to find.
But in certain studios and fitting rooms around the country, tape measures are wielded, fabric is pinched and pinned and the warmth of service extends well beyond holding out an Eftpos machine.

For hand-makers, the work is about more than just another product or a paycheck. The beauty of their vocation is in many small acts: mastering technique, appreciating texture, building a community of clients, and drawing on the mysterious well of creative intuition that allows humans to make wonderful things.

highlights.title: Is selling an AI version of your face to this microdrama startup the future of Hollywood?
highlights.summary: An actor has licensed his face to a microdrama startup — in a trend that's already popular in China. Experts question the long-term consequences if this becomes a trend in Hollywood, too.
body: For the most part, the content offered by the microdrama startup Shortical is indistinguishable from the rest of its industry. The company produces soapy, melodramatic storylines — almost always risqué romances — that, in bite-sized two-minute episodes, compel viewers to stay glued to their phones so as not to miss the latest twist in a tawdry, cliff-hanger-happy saga.

The primary way that Shortical — which was founded last January — makes money is through subscriptions. Typically, the first 7-10 episodes of a micro-drama are free. After that, if the user wants to finish the series, they have to pay a small monthly fee which unlocks access to all of the site’s content.

Over the past year, the company has churned out a gush of popular live-action romances like “Crossing the Line with My Neighbor,” “Accidentally Married My Boss,” and “Spoiled by My Billionaire Sugar Daddy.”

Lately, however, the company’s homepage is covered in AI-generated content. The reason isn’t exactly hard to figure out: the production overhead for AI content is substantially less than live-action. The profit potential, meanwhile, is substantially higher, if you can draw an audience.
points: An actor has licensed his face to a microdrama startup — in a trend that's already popular in China.
Experts question the long-term consequences if this becomes a trend in Hollywood, too.

The project has cycled through several writers. Damon Lindelof ( Lost, The Leftovers, Watchmen ) and Justin Britt-Gibson were the original screenwriters before Disney fired them — the pair are currently working together on HBO’s superhero detective series, Lanterns. body: Russell Brand is selling merchandise calling for his freedom while he’s behind bars after being sentenced to 10 years and six months in prison after being found guilty of rape and sexual assault.

“So Russell has asked me to read something to you today,” the actor’s wife said at the start of the video, before looking to a notebook to read her husband’s message. “Beloved brothers and sisters in Christ, God bless you for your support. Brand was sentenced to 10 years and six months in prison after being found guilty of rape and sexual assault. The trial lasted four weeks at Southwark Crown Court, with the jury finding him guilty on one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault (he was found not guilty on two other rape charges and not guilty of attempted indecent assault).

The actor has three items featuring “Free Russell” available for purchase on the website for Reborn, his wellness business. Every item is available for $34.99; a shirt with the words “Free Russell Brand “; a hat with the same text; and another shirt that reads “Free Russell” with an image of himself.

highlights.title: The moment I knew: She flew me to the scene of my favourite romantic movie
highlights.summary: Kaz Therese had always loved An Affair to Remember. A few months into their relationship, Brianna surprised her with a magical gift. Find more stories from the moment I knew series.
body: Brianna and I met in 2013 on an arts project I was developing in Mount Druitt, the region I grew up in, in western Sydney.
It was a site-specific work for young people, and Brianna became part of the strategic leadership team, which ultimately meant she was painting gutters pink with the local kids until 9pm each night.

Our first meeting was electric – we had so much in common, I felt as if I’d been donged on the head. Through the work, I was trying to push back against the stigma of Mount Druitt and create something fun and magical, and she understood the importance of what I was trying to do. After the project, I got a position running a theatre company nearby, and I invited her on to the board.

We were both in relationships at the time and I was coming out of a deeply unhappy one. For those first two years working together, I had a secret crush on her. A few months later we were both single and I invited her over to help write a grant together for a project I hoped to do in Berlin. That week happened to be my birthday, and a friend had given me a bottle of Moët, which I planned to save for a special occasion.

“Have you always dreamed of abusing your power without consequence?” one spot begins. “Well, now you can, when you join the Vice City Police Department, VCPD. You’ll have fun learning the ins and outs of applying excessive force.” The commercial goes on to suggest that cadets will be trained in racial profiling and planting evidence.

Given that blistering analysis of American law enforcement, you might imagine that actual cops aren’t big fans of the latest GTA title, which was released after a 13-year wait on Thursday. Yet as millions of gamers have started to explore every stash house and back alley in the sun-drenched wilderness of a fictionalized South Florida, even police departments have attempted to exploit this monocultural mania to elevate their public messaging or recruit new officers.

highlights.summary: Who wouldn’t love to have a few chores taken off their hands? This holiday season, give someone you love one of the most useful gifts: a brand-new robot vacuum that will leave floors sparkling.
body: I test a lot of robot vacuums and have used an Ecovacs robot vacuum in my home for years. I absolutely love their reliability, innovative designs, and competitive prices. Even if I haven’t had a chance to try the Deebot T90 Pro Omni just yet, it’s sure to deliver an incredible clean, and honestly, all those high-end features under $600 are pretty unheard of.

One of my biggest issues with robot vacuums is their lack of power to pick up larger, heavier messes, especially on deep-pile carpets and rugs. The 30,000Pa boosted suction power is the highest I’ve seen and will remove more debris than your typical robot vacuum. Noise-reducing tech is built in to help keep things quieter. The roller also extends 0.6 inches beyond the body, letting it reach edges, baseboards, and more.

Mopping shouldn’t disappoint either, thanks in large part to the Ozmo 3.0 roller system. The mop self-cleans while scrubbing floors with continuous pressure rather than just wiping like typical mopping pads. The roller also lifts on carpets and rugs, so you won’t need to deal with nasty wet edges. AI tech even helps the robot vacuum precisely weave around obstacles, including pets, while cleaning.

highlights.title: Too lazy for lawns? Try a native meadow
highlights.summary: Exotic lawns require a tradeoff between ease and beauty. While Australian native grasses take longer to establish, they can be worth the wait. Get our weekend culture and lifestyle email. Do you yearn for that suburban dream, the perfect lawn?
body: Do you yearn to join one of those neighbourhood groups whose members compete to show off the result – the kind of people who use laser levels and precision bombing with biological weapons to achieve grassy perfection?
“There’s no grass that ticks all the boxes,” says Melbourne landscaper Simon McCurdy. “Each has its positive attributes and drawbacks.”

In his 38 years of experience, McCurdy has seen roll-out turf largely displace seed-sowing for lawn establishment. “Virtually all our clients want instant results,” he says. “And when you factor in the time involved in sowing from seed it’s certainly cheaper for most people to install turf.”

For larger areas McCurdy says many people choose hydroseeding, an intermediate method between seeding and turf, in which emulsions of seed, water, mulch and fertiliser are sprayed on to prepared soil. But which grass variety to choose?

highlights.title: International UN talks on controlling use of autonomous weapons collapse
highlights.summary: Week-long efforts fail to establish negotiating mandate on AI warfare after Russian ‘filibustering’ Week-long efforts to agree a negotiating mandate for a legally binding international treaty to control the use of autonomous weapons collapsed just before 5am after all-night talks failed to overcome…
body: Despite an overwhelming majority of states at the UN’s Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons (CCW) in Geneva wanting to agree a negotiating mandate leading to a legally binding treaty, the need for consensus forced the conference to adopt a much weaker option.
The mandate asked countries “to elaborate by consensus”, an instrument that may not carry any legal obligations.

Although Russia led the objections using obstructive stalling tactics, other military powers invested in AI warfare, such as the US, were reluctant to commit to a legally binding protocol protecting civilians from robot drones and other autonomous weapons.

Some argued that international humanitarian law was sufficient. More than 100 states had been pushing for a new law, saying the weapons raised entirely new challenges. European and Nato states, including Ukraine, China and Iran, expressed support or willingness for a new protocol.
